12.technique: RouterBench evaluation framework with AIQ metric and Zero router baseline
12.how: Routers are points in the cost-quality plane. Mixing two routers with probability t gives any point on their segment; extrapolation adds cost without quality. The non-decreasing convex hull is the Zero router; AIQ is hull area over [cmin, cmax] divided by the cost span. KNN and MLP routers pick argmax of lambda times predicted quality minus cost; the cascade calls models cheapest first until a judge passes.
12.effect: Oracle: MMLU 0.957 at $0.297 vs GPT-4 0.828 at $4.086; HellaSwag 0.994 at $0.86 vs GPT-4 0.923 at $24.29. Predictive AIQ vs Zero: MMLU 0.773/0.769 vs 0.763; ARC 0.871/0.875 vs 0.877; MBPP 0.644/0.642 vs 0.660; HellaSwag 0.588 all. Cascade at zero error: MMLU 0.901, MBPP 0.862, ARC 0.923, GSM8K 0.680 (Zero 0.628), HellaSwag 0.469 vs Zero 0.607. RAG AIQ: KNN 0.695, MLP 0.675, cascade 0.657, Zero 0.632.
12.loses: Cost and quality only, no latency. Mostly academic multiple-choice tasks, 2023-era models, no coding agents or long contexts. Cost for predictive routers approximated by per-token price. Cascade judge is simulated with perfect knowledge, so results are an upper bound. Three tasks graded by GPT-4. RAG has few models and one client's queries. In-domain train and test split; out-domain test only plotted.

12.technique: Fine-tuned 350M SLM for tool calling (SFT with TRL)
12.how: Supervised fine-tuning of facebook/opt-350m for 1 epoch (HF TRL SFTTrainer) on ToolBench converted to 187,542 Thought/Action/Action Input examples; LR 5e-5, effective batch 32, FP16, gradient checkpointing, 5,860 steps.
12.effect: Pass rate 77.55% overall vs ToolLLaMA-DFS 30.18%, ChatGPT-CoT 26.00%, ToolLLaMA-CoT 16.27%, Claude-CoT 2.73%; 74.0-80.5% across categories.
12.loses: Training data and evaluation tightly coupled; may not generalize beyond ToolBench; controlled API set; retraining needed as APIs evolve; still needs compute and data.

12.technique: LiteLLM budget caps, Langfuse, LLMLingua, RouteLLM, GPTCache semantic cache
12.how: Roundup: LiteLLM max_budget per key; LLMLingua prompt compression; RouteLLM routes between two models by threshold; GPTCache semantic caching.
12.effect: RouteLLM 85% cost reduction keeping 95% GPT-4 quality on MT Bench (45% MMLU, 35% GSM8K); LongLLMLingua +21.4% RAG with 1/4 tokens.
12.loses: Vendor blog citing others' numbers; RouteLLM is binary routing only.

12.technique: GraphRouter heterogeneous graph router (task/query/LLM nodes, edge prediction)
12.how: Heterogeneous graph with task, query and LLM nodes; initial embeddings from a GPT-4o description encoded by BERT. Edges task-query and LLM-query (performance, cost). 2-layer GAT, 32-dim hidden. Trained by edge prediction; inference picks argmax dot product. Reward = alpha*Perf - beta*Cost with (alpha,beta) = (1,0), (0.5,0.5), (0.2,0.8).
12.effect: Performance-First reward 0.539 vs FrugalGPT 0.517, oracle 0.588; Balance 0.209 vs 0.196 (oracle 0.231); Cost-First 0.064 vs 0.057 (oracle 0.072); Claims >=12.28% reward gain and >=88.89% of oracle; Performance-First table gain is ~4%; New LLMs few-shot 0.207 vs C2MAB-V 0.189 (+9.52%), time cost -99.45%
12.loses: Exploratory; no path or taxonomy signals; LLMs handle numeric price and context info poorly; small 4-task benchmark.

12.technique: Arch-Router preference-aligned domain-action routing (1.5B model)
12.how: A 1.5B model maps each prompt to user-defined domain and action routes, each tied to a preferred model, without retraining when models change.
12.effect: Claims state-of-the-art preference matching on conversational data; no cost figure in this page.
12.loses: Routes by declared preference, not measured cost; accuracy numbers not on this page.

12.technique: Cost-Spectrum Contrastive Routing (CSCR): shared embedding plus FAISS k-NN
12.how: Cost-Spectrum Contrastive Routing: prompts (frozen MiniLM + MLP head) and models embedded in one space. Models described by logit footprints (open models) or perplexity fingerprints (black-box APIs). Cost-Spectrum InfoNCE: banded positives (K=5), band-specific temperatures, cost-weighted negatives (gamma=0.2). Routing is one FAISS k-NN lookup.
12.effect: Best AUDC on all three benchmarks; up to 25% better accuracy-cost trade-off. OOD AUDC 0.5146 vs next-best 0.4863. Cost-aware loss lifts AUDC 0.342 to 0.495 and peak accuracy 36% to 54% (ablation).
12.loses: Did not test large pools. Perplexity descriptor is at least 2x slower. Cost-aware training raises cost versus vanilla variant.

12.technique: Two-stage cascade: confidence deferral policy then abstention policy, online-learned
12.how: Two-tier cascade Mbase -> Mlarge -> human. Verification confidence from surrogate token probability YES/(YES+NO) (also self-verification, consistent self-verification, MC-dropout STP), calibrated by Bayesian logistic regression on 100 samples; posterior mean is confidence, posterior std is uncertainty. Defer if confidence <= phi_base; abstain if uncertainty > xi. Thresholds tuned online by Adam on a soft-masked system risk 1-E[Correct]+lc*E[Cost]+la*P(abstain).
12.effect: Cascade has lower cumulative regret than either single model on 4 of 5 datasets; MedQA unclear; Verifying with the large model gives better delta-IBC; on ARC2-simple delta-IBC up to 258.4 +-39.1 with large-model verification vs about -2 to -37 with base; Calibration set size 50-500 samples makes no significant difference; Label flipping in calibration raises regret
12.loses: Sensitive to cost and abstention weights (trivial solutions); initialisation affects convergence; needs human feedback; MedQA no gain; multiple-choice QA only.

12.technique: RouterEval benchmark and oracle-router analysis (model-level scaling)
12.how: RouterEval: router as m-way classifier over an input embedding predicting a one-hot or multi-hot best-LLM vector. Splits 8:1:1; simple m in {3,5}, hard m in {10,100,1000}.
12.effect: A router with p>=0.5 of matching the oracle improves quickly with candidates; about 3-10 candidates most cost-effective, can approach GPT-4 reference with weak models. Existing routers have VR<=1 and VB<=1. Some routers have Ep 0.00-0.03 (collapse to one model).
12.loses: Accuracy only; cost objective deferred; most records not open source; data volume too small for a strong router.

12.technique: Inference production frontier (cost-quality Pareto, optimal concurrency zone)
12.how: Cost per test = hourly GPU cost x wall time. Hourly cost = depreciation + power + maintenance (about $0.79/h per A800; cloud $2.82-5.64/h). Sweep serving concurrency to find the cheapest setting that still meets throughput (>20 tok/s) and TTFT (<1s) limits.
12.effect: WiNGPT-3.5 concurrency 8->48: total time 2034s->774s; 48 optimal. WiNGPT-3.5 76.2 at $0.34 vs Seed-OSS-36B 72.2 at $0.55. Thinking model WiNGPT-3.0 emits 3.44M output tokens vs about 0.35-1.4M for others.
12.loses: No training cost or capex, hardware-stack dependent, proxy benchmark, no confidence intervals, weak link to API billing.

12.technique: Auto Router: eligibility filter, difficulty classification, quality-vs-cost scoring, session affinity
12.how: Filters eligible models, classifies task type and difficulty, ranks by quality versus cost, falls back down the list; session-id header keeps one model per turn for caching.
12.effect: not measured; sticky session lets requests reuse prompt cache.
12.loses: Without session id, requests may switch models and lose cache; no savings number.

12.technique: Session affinity for cache hits; cache and difficulty-aware routing; batch tier
12.how: Keeps an agent on the same server so its context stays cached; routing is cache- and difficulty-aware; Batch is 50% off.
12.effect: Cache hit rates up to 99.6% in long agent sessions; cached input at half price or less; cache writes free.
12.loses: Vendor marketing claims; a customer quote of $4M to $800K is anecdotal.

12.technique: Cascade routing (unified routing plus cascading, proven optimal)
12.how: Routing is a linear program. Theorem 1: the optimum is gamma*s_MIN + (1-gamma)*s_MAX at the lambda that meets the budget, found by binary search over lambda. Cascading is sequential routing over supermodels M_1:i (Theorem 2). Cascade routing picks among all supermodels containing the models already run (Theorem 3), with supermodel quality E[max member quality] and cost summed. Lemma 1 prunes negative-marginal-gain models.
12.effect: Table 1 0-shot AUC at 11 models Low/Med/High: routing 83.25/74.63/72.67, cascade baseline 84.48/73.64/69.79, cascade ours 84.47/75.10/70.26, cascade routing 87.24/77.57/74.40. Gains up to 8% over cascading and 12% over routing. SWE-Bench: 54.12 vs routing 40.47 (10 models). Realistic noisy estimators: 1.2% mean gain. Runtime 15 ms; Greedy 1.4 ms with 0.5-1.3 point loss.
12.loses: Gains depend on estimate quality; with poor estimators cascade routing only matches routing. Quality estimators are trained per model and per computed-model history. Up to 2^k supermodels; Normal handles 40 models in 1 s, Max-Depth 3 handles 80. Hyperparameter search is harder for cascades; in 5-shot low-noise cascade ours trails the baseline in two of three cases.

12.technique: LLM-to-SLM agent conversion algorithm (S1-S6)
12.how: S1-S6 conversion recipe: log non-HCI agent calls; curate and filter (10k-100k examples, remove PII); cluster tasks; select SLM; fine-tune (LoRA/QLoRA/full, optional distillation); iterate and retrain SLMs and router.
12.effect: Cited from other work: 7B SLM 10-30x cheaper than 70-175B LLM. Authors estimate replaceable LLM queries: MetaGPT about 60%, Open Operator about 40%, Cradle about 70%.
12.loses: No measured savings; estimates are the authors'; acknowledges centralized LLM inference may still be cheaper per token (jury still out).

12.technique: SLM-default, LLM-fallback with uncertainty routing, verifiers, Cost per Successful task (CPS)
12.how: SLM-default routing: small model with guided decoding and validators handles the task; uncertainty or validation failure escalates to a large model. Track Cost per Successful task (CPS) and schema validity; rollback thresholds trigger fallback.
12.effect: Body claims 10-30x lower cost; abstract says 10x-100x (inconsistent).; Table II is placeholder data.
12.loses: Not a controlled experiment; headline factors unmeasured.

12.technique: Premium request multipliers and monthly allowance
12.how: Premium models consume allowance with multipliers; overages billed per request; budgets can be set.
12.effect: Reasoning models may consume 5x or 20x the standard rate.
12.loses: Legacy billing for annual plans only after June 2026.

12.technique: Router-R1 RL-trained multi-round router with cost reward
12.how: Router is a 3B LLM policy trained with PPO that interleaves think with search calls to a pool of 6 LLMs (max 4 routing steps). Reward = format + (1-alpha)*EM outcome + alpha*cost; hierarchical (format failure zeroes others); cost normalized with sliding-window percentiles. New LLMs added via descriptors without retraining.
12.effect: Average EM 0.416 (Qwen router) and 0.409 (Llama router) above baselines.; Adding two unseen LLMs: average EM 0.458 to 0.463 without retraining.; Average API calls about 1.01-1.36.; Alpha 0.6-0.9: performance falls as cost reward rises; emergent small-first then escalate.
12.loses: QA only with Exact Match; cost reward studied only for QA; router itself costs 3B inference per step; no cost-weighted Pareto in the main table.

12.technique: Causal (CATE-corrected) router training mixing gold and preference labels
12.how: Pairwise router (premium vs cheap). Bias between preference-based (PB) and gold-standard (GS) labels is a CATE, estimated with R- or DR-learners; pseudo-GS labels y+bias train a regressor on GS plus corrected PB. Route to premium if predicted gain exceeds cost factor w. GS scale normalised to PB scale.
12.effect: PB-GS difference mean significantly below 0 (p<2.2e-16); Meta-routers gain most when GS data is scarce; PRBench: DR-learner best at small n
12.loses: GS labels from an LLM judge not experts; pairwise only; needs overlapping query support; no headline cost number in text.

12.technique: Learned post-hoc deferral rule on token-level uncertainty quantiles (LM cascade)
12.how: Two-model cascade (FLAN-T5 Base to Large). Deferral score from token-level uncertainty: Chow-Sum, Chow-Average, Chow-Quantile (quantiles of per-token probabilities), and a learned post-hoc MLP (5 layers, 32 units) on quantile features, optionally plus small-model and large-model intermediate embeddings.
12.effect: Chow-Sum defers long outputs, Chow-Average defers short ones (length bias). Post-hoc rule is consistently best or near-best on AUC-DF. Using large-model first-token embedding helps most on classification.
12.loses: Only FLAN-T5 encoder-decoder; decoder-only and RLHF-calibration effects untested. Intermediate large-model embeddings add non-trivial cost. No single best quantile across tasks.

12.technique: RouterArena router leaderboard (accuracy vs cost metrics, 12 routers)
12.how: RouterArena: Arena score=(1+b)AC/(bA+C), log2-normalised cost, b=0.1, cmin 0.0044, cmax 200 per 1k queries.
12.effect: MIRT-BERT 66.9, Azure-Router 66.7, NIRT-BERT 66.1, GPT-5 64.3, vLLM-SR 64.3, CARROT 63.9, RouterDC 33.8; oracle 90.89%. NIRT-BERT ~378% of best model cost; vLLM-SR/CARROT ~35% cheaper under 2% loss; MIRT-BERT ~5x optimal.
12.loses: One-shot queries, not agents.

12.technique: Execution-verified downgrade-and-cascade step-level routing labels
12.how: Step-level router mapping a trajectory prefix to a tier (low, mid, mid_high, high). Labels come from a greedy sequential-locking downgrade search: from a successful strong trajectory, try tiers cheapest-up at each step and accept if the full trajectory still passes with no more LLM-call steps. Three-model tier cascade verification; failure-aware COST SAVE; bill = API cost + (1-resolved)*$0.60.
12.effect: Dynamic: trained router resolved 75/100 at $25.66 vs unrouted Opus 4.6 74/100 at $54.73 (-53.1% API cost); Rule-based variant cost $172.56 (6.7x more than trained router); Opus 4.6 as a router predicted high for only 7 of 147 verified-high SWE steps; Cascade recovered 28 of 33 downgradeable labels vs 15 of 33 for single-model probing
12.loses: Small static corpus; greedy search may miss cross-step interactions; labels tied to a fixed pool and price snapshot; dynamic track SWE-bench Verified only (Astropy and Django); English only.

12.technique: Premium request model multipliers (code review = 13)
12.how: Each prompt uses one premium request times the model's rate; Copilot code review consumes 13 from June 1 2026.
12.effect: not measured
12.loses: Applies to legacy annual plans only.

12.technique: LLMRouterBench unified routing evaluation (Best Single and Oracle baselines, Pareto analysis)
12.how: Benchmark and framework with Collector, Evaluator, Adaptor. 21 datasets, 33 models, 391,645 instances, 23,945 prompts, ~1.8B tokens, $2,771.84 API cost, ~1K GPU hours. Two settings: performance-oriented (20 ~7B models, 15 datasets) and performance-cost (13 flagship models, 10 datasets). 10 routers compared; metrics AvgAcc, Gain@R/B, Gap@O, PerfGain, CostSave, ParetoDist.
12.effect: Best routers: up to +4% AvgAcc and up to 31.7% cost reduction vs GPT-5 (Best Single) at matched accuracy; OpenRouter -24.7% PerfGain, fails to match; Model-recall failure: when <=3 experts are right (410 queries, 11.9%), Avengers 24.6%, EmbedLLM 23.2%; Latency: Qwen3-Thinking vs GLM-4.6 similar cost and accuracy but 262.1s vs 32.4s
12.loses: Not all routers covered; excludes long-context, multimodal, vertical domains; latency approximate via OpenRouter throughput.

12.technique: BayesianRouter (offline multi-task router prior plus online Thompson sampling)
12.how: Offline: SmolLM2-135M encoder over (prompt, response pair) with MLP on [e+e'; |e-e'|]; Bradley-Terry head on reward-model disagreement pairs plus auxiliary per-RM classification head, L = L_bt + lambda L_cls. Online: Bayesian linear Thompson sampling per query, Sigma^-1 += hh^T/sigma^2, offline BT embedding as prior mean; reward is negative DPO loss, quantile-normalised.
12.effect: AlpacaEval-2 63.23 vs best single RM 61.86 and LASER 60.50; GSM8K 75.66; MMLU 57.39; Offline router OOD accuracy 87.92 vs ~87.65 best single (RewardBench 2, 2,939 pairs); LinUCB collapses to a single arm
12.loses: DPO only (PPO untested); gap to oracle remains; slightly slower than the fastest single RM; gains modest.

12.technique: Speculative cascades (deferral rule implemented via speculative execution)
12.how: Speculative cascades. Drafter q proposes gamma tokens; verifier p scores them in parallel. A token-level deferral rule (Chow, Diff, OPT, or token-specific V1-V3) sets target (1-delta)q + delta*p. GenSpecSample (Algorithm 4) generalizes speculative sampling to that target. Lossy SD is a special case.
12.effect: Table 2 (T=1, gamma=5, Small to Large) latency reduction at large-model quality, WMT/XSum/CNNDM: SpecDecode[Lossy] 1.61/1.10/1.57x; SpecCascade[OPT] 1.95/1.17/1.80x; Token 1.85/1.18/1.89x. Best quality at large-model latency, WMT BLEU: Lossy 17.26, OPT 18.33, Token 22.50.
12.loses: Two-model setup only. Higher total compute than sequential cascades. Plug-in estimators need calibrated models. Objective is local per position. Batch size 1, TPU. Evaluation protocol differs from standard SD. No fairness analysis. Paper claims no new state of the art. OPT weaker on Gemma than T5.

12.technique: Mixture-of-Agents (layered proposers and aggregators)
12.how: Layered proposers and aggregators: y_i = concat_j A_ij(x_i) + x_1, each layer's models see all previous outputs through an Aggregate-and-Synthesize prompt. Default 6 open models, 3 layers, Qwen1.5-110B-Chat final aggregator. MoA-Lite is 2 layers with Qwen1.5-72B aggregator.
12.effect: MoA 65.1+-0.6% LC win; MoA w/ GPT-4o 65.7%; MoA-Lite 59.3%; GPT-4o 57.5%; MoA-Lite matches GPT-4o cost with +1.8 points; MoA-Lite beats GPT-4 Turbo (55.0%) by ~4% at over 2x cost-effectiveness; 6 proposers 61.3% vs 1 proposer 47.8%
12.loses: High time-to-first-token (last layer must finish). First aggregation layer gives most gain. LLM ranker much worse than aggregation.

12.technique: Comp-LLM (sub-query dependency graph with embedding-similarity expert assignment)
12.how: Comp-LLM: decomposer (SFT Llama 2 7B on 1000 GPT-4o examples) -> expert router (mean-pooled embedding, cosine, sq_sim 0.7 else base model) -> DAG scheduler running ready sub-queries in parallel -> aggregator; LoRA experts.
12.effect: Comp-LLM (35B) F1 0.78 vs Llama-2 70B 0.79, Mixtral 0.74, OLMoE 0.52. Decomposer F1 0.87/0.86 vs few-shot 0.48/0.42. 108.78s vs 892.07s for offloaded Llama-2-70B on one A40; latency 1.1x-1.7x vs sequential.
12.loses: Needs experts per domain, static reasoning only, measures size not dollars.

12.technique: Application-specific capability profiling testbed (cost-aware model selection per application)
12.how: Eight-step profiling method, Stage 1 built as testbed: sparse versioned model profile where missing never equals zero; comparability only for same attribute, context and dataset; evidence levels L0-L4; Pareto set with evidence counts; plan gate with SHA-256 plan hash and baseline arm; null-agent check; range noise rule with three-state verdict; fail-closed reporting. Constrained model-to-task-part selection (Eq. 11) is planned, not built.
12.effect: Migration fully-correct 98 to 108 of 216 (45.4 to 50.0%, Fisher p=0.39); accepted-but-wrong or unverifiable 9.7% to 21.9% (p=0.023); about 78% of ok verdicts proved nothing. Breadth: agent 91.9% vs cheap 90.5% (p=0.21); agent used 3.0% fewer tokens. Automation: model effect p=0.007, framework p=0.40; tokens 1,953-9,465; CrewAI about 4x. Judge churn 16.2% at T=0; full run $3-4.
12.loses: Stage 1 only; model-vs-framework comparisons are non-causal separate sweeps. Migration inference unpaired, no multiplicity correction. Only P1 and chatbot integrated as probes; Grafana JSON never imported. Adapter-generation hook unevaluated. 15 automation samples unreadable. Caller key crosses a process boundary unprotected. Range rule loses power as repeats grow.

12.technique: LLM-assisted labeling then fine-tuned small NER model (GLiNER, SpanMarker)
12.how: Uses a large LLM to label data, then fine-tunes a compact model for the task and deploys it on a cheap endpoint.
12.effect: Up to 6.4% accuracy gain and up to 80x cheaper inference than large LLMs for financial NER.
12.loses: Needs labeled data and training; narrow task, not general agent work.

12.technique: Retained reasoning plus native compaction, programmatic tool calling, low reasoning effort, small-tier model (Luna) selection
12.how: Persists reasoning across turns with compaction, runs tool orchestration in code outside context, and uses cheaper tiers or lower effort.
12.effect: ARC-AGI-3 13.3% to 38.3% with about 6x fewer output tokens; BrowseComp 84.04% at $1.33 versus 84.36% at $33.27 for GPT-5.5; PlayerZero cost -64%.
12.loses: Vendor and customer testimonials; harness-specific.

12.technique: OpenRouter provider routing (effective price with real cache hit rate, sort, max_price, :floor/:nitro, fallbacks)
12.how: Picks a provider per request by measured effective price reflecting its cache hit rate, throughput, latency and reliability; supports sort, max_price and fallbacks.
12.effect: Not measured; reacts to provider changes within minutes.
12.loses: Provider choice not model choice; bypassed when order or own keys set.

12.technique: Rule-first classifier plus decision model with probability threshold (0.85) routing fast versus frontier tier, per-tier API key budgets
12.how: Explicit rules first, then a decision model picks tier; fast tier accepted only if probability >= 0.85, else frontier; AI Gateway fallbacks and spend caps per tier.
12.effect: Not measured; threshold 0.85 given as an example.
12.loses: Experimental Decision API; threshold needs tuning.

12.technique: RLM-Cascade (complexity router, cheap draft model, Opus verify or skip)
12.how: Local proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL) with a rule-based O(1) router, no model calls. Requests with a non-empty tools field go straight to Opus. Simple prefixes go to the cheap model only (SKIPPED). Complex keywords or input over 1,500 chars get cheap draft then Opus verify (USE_DRAFT = ACCEPTED, or ENHANCE).
12.effect: Savings 45.8% (service, N=125), 47.4% (architecture set, N=39), 32% (current run, N=12); model predicted 67.2% vs 47.4% observed. p50 latency 2,026 vs 3,698 ms. Quality 100% vs 95% pass (N=20).
12.loses: Tool-selection turns (70-80% of Claude Code turns) bypass to Opus, so savings apply to the ~20-30% text turns. Router is a keyword classifier. One cost inversion (+$0.01189). TTFT 2.1x worse. Learned router, parallel draft+verify, local tier are future work.

12.technique: Cache-aware cost comparison with TCO model and hybrid routing counterfactual replay
12.how: Longitudinal case study: Langfuse and vLLM telemetry plus Git mining. Fix Commit Ratio via regex over commit messages; difficulty-stratified Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio; TCO = M x (compute + ops + T_iter x wage); hybrid-routing offline counterfactual replay by difficulty tier.
12.effect: 99.3% cache hit cut API cost 88.6% to $0.57/M tokens vs $2.83/M shared on-prem; FCR 74.9% vs 45.9%; Mantel-Haenszel OR 3.61; Shared on-prem saves 40.1% true TCO; dedicated costs 43.8% more; High-to-Claude hybrid saves 26.3%
12.loses: One developer, non-randomized, tasks differ between periods; keyword-classified fixes; Period A fix count inflated by CI work; replay assumes tier exchangeability.

12.technique: PORT: training-free online routing via ANN query-feature estimation plus one-time dual optimisation
12.how: PORT: kNN (5 neighbours) estimate perf and cost; random-route first eps=0.025 queries; solve dual gamma* once; route to argmax(alpha*d - gamma*_i*g); queue when budget exhausted. Competitive ratio 1-O(eps+delta).
12.effect: Avg 3.55x performance, 1.85x cost efficiency, ~4.25x throughput. Vs BatchSplit +33% perf, +38% cost efficiency. Reaches 75.99-84.66% of approximate optimum.
12.loses: Only perf and cost modelled; needs labelled history; assumes similar queries behave alike and random order.

12.technique: RouterDC: encoder plus LLM embeddings trained with sample-LLM and sample-sample contrastive losses
12.how: RouterDC: encoder plus learnable LLM embeddings, trained with sample-LLM and sample-sample contrastive losses; route a query to the LLM whose embedding is most similar. Clustering similar queries stabilises training.
12.effect: Average 58.54 vs 54.56 (+3.98) in-distribution; OOD 45.85 vs 43.95 (+1.90).; About 6x faster than voting.
12.loses: Needs scored training data per candidate LLM. Limitations section only says scenarios are left to future work.

12.technique: Self-MoA and sequential Self-MoA (aggregate samples from one top model)
12.how: Self-MoA samples N outputs from the single best model (temperature 0.7); one aggregator synthesises them. Self-MoA-Seq aggregates with a sliding window of 6 responses. Regression of mixture performance on quality and Vendi-score diversity.
12.effect: AlpacaEval LC: Self-MoA 65.7 vs Mixed-MoA 59.1 (+6.6); Quality coefficient exceeds diversity coefficient (MMLU 2.558 vs 1.841); Self-MoA with TaskBest averages +3.8%
12.loses: Mixed-MoA wins when models are similar in quality and complementary; gains not monotonic in samples; aggregator context limit.

12.technique: Bayesian aggregation of multi-LLM likelihoods with expected-utility and value-of-information gating
12.how: Elicit p(evidence|state) from M LLMs via contrastive 'assume state s' prompts, aggregate by median, apply Bayes with deployment prior, choose action by minimum expected cost, gather more evidence if value of information exceeds its cost or models disagree.
12.effect: $294,000 (34%) lower total cost vs best single-LLM; parity gap 22 to 5 points. Ablation shares: multi-LLM 51%, sequential 43%, disagreement-triggered screening 20%. 20 LLM queries per observation (M=5, K=4).
12.loses: Synthetic data and simulated screens; latency of 20 queries per step; cost matrix assumed; model IDs and versions inconsistent between abstract and appendix.

12.technique: Harness-level cost and Pass@1 benchmark with a cost-calibrated Lite-80 subset
12.how: Adapter protocol (create_agent, send_task, backup_session, delete_agent, get_docker_args); patch exported from git diff; history after base_commit removed to stop leakage. Lite-80 subset picked by quartile-quota local search with ranking hinge and cost-parity filter.
12.effect: Bare adapter 19.3% vs full adapter 71.2% resolved; largest harness gap at fixed model 24.3 pp; Best Pass@1 Hermes Agent 81.7% at $36; Lite-80 vs full: MAE 0.81 pp at 25.3% of cost
12.loses: Meta-Harness evolved and evaluated on same instances; Lite is a proxy; appendix F is single-run.

12.technique: Shapley-value cost attribution of thinking tokens and turns; price reversal
12.how: Cost c = p_in*n_in + p_out*n_out (+ cache terms for agents). Shapley-value attribution of the cost gap between two models over eight multilinear factors (turns, input, output, cache, thinking tokens, and three prices), with a closed form. Cost treated as a distribution with quantile-level reversal analysis.
12.effect: 106 of 336 pairs (32%) show price reversal; 11% on ArenaHard to 57% on MMLU-Pro; Gemini 3 Flash: 80% lower listed price than GPT-5.4 but 38% higher total cost ($705 vs $509); Single-turn: thinking tokens over 95% of the gap; agentic: turns over 80% (Kimi vs GPT-5.4); Repeat-run cost on the same query varies up to 9.7x
12.loses: Costs only, no quality; one price snapshot (May 2026); cost prediction left open; no limitations section.

12.technique: Cost-of-pass and frontier cost-of-pass metric
12.how: cost-of-pass v(m,p) = C_m(p)/R_m(p), the expected cost of one correct answer (assumes independent trials). Frontier cost-of-pass V_p(M) is the minimum over models plus a human-expert baseline. Gain is the reduction when a model is added; family essentialness is the relative frontier increase when a family is removed. Exponential decay fit gives a halving time.
12.effect: Frontier cost-of-pass halves every 2.6 months (MATH-500) and 7.1 months (AIME24); Essentialness: lightweight 93.5% (two-digit addition); reasoning 74.4% (MATH500) and 81.0% (AIME24); large models matter on knowledge tasks (GPQA 33.3%, BBQ 44.7%); Majority voting yields 0% relative gain everywhere; self-refine 24.9% on GPQA; TALE-EP 66.6% on GSM8K
12.loses: Binary pass/fail and expectation only (no variance); ignores verification, retry and tool costs; contamination possible; single prompt setting; i.i.d. retry assumption is contested (A:123); only 16 Tau-bench tasks.

12.technique: Task-based auto model routing along cache boundaries with 10% credit discount
12.how: Scores the task on reasoning, code complexity, bug difficulty and tool needs plus model health, then picks a model; routes along cache boundaries.
12.effect: Paid users get 10% fewer AI credits; vendor says token efficiency improves with no quality regression (no numbers).

27.how: Reward r_final = alpha*r_tool*r_correct (multiplicative; additive was unstable because the model gained reward by calling fewer tools without a correct answer). 27.technique: Restart Economics: retry priced by cost per resolved task, iteration cap as a guard, break-even in median attempt costs
27.how: Restart Economics: expected cost per incoming task, with agent spend, verification and a priced outside option (annotated engineer time). Policy ladder: no retry, retry with best attempt budget (K at most 4), retry with a per-attempt iteration cap, schedules by coordinate ascent, a receding-horizon restart rule on three state variables, and cascades across configurations. Exact replay of truncated logged trajectories scores each policy. Break-even is stated in multiples of the median attempt cost.
27.effect: Automated verifier, $100 an hour: retry cuts expected cost 13.2 to 19.6% for six configurations and 4.3% for GPT-5.2; at $300 an hour 16.4 to 21.0% (GPT-5.2 8.0%). Dollar savings per task at $100 an hour: GPT-5 5.67 [3.42, 8.80], GPT-5.2 1.01 [0.45, 2.16]. The iteration cap adds nothing given retry: break-even 2.14 to 3.83 median attempt costs ($1.74 to $7.08 an hour); margin never distinct from zero on the cost side in any of 532 cells; best hindsight cap saves at most $0.03 per task. Attempts still running at 100 calls resolve 33 to 55% of the time. Only 11 to 25% of tasks have mixed outcomes. Cross-configuration outcome correlation 0.62 to 0.90. Cascades save 9.2% in point estimate at $100 an hour, interval includes zero. Review at 0.5 of the outside option: no configuration retries, the cap saves $0.75 to $3.56 per task at $100 an hour. The fitted state rule stops 42 to 78% too early and costs 7 to 32% more than the exact optimum on synthetic attempts.
27.loses: Clean restarts only. One benchmark, one harness (OpenHands CodeActAgent), at most 4 attempts. A configuration is not a model. SWE-bench Verified contamination. The outside option is annotated time, understated for short tasks. The state rule has 8 coefficients; learned monitors are untested. Working paper v0.1, single author, not peer reviewed.
